place_name: Dzukou Valley (Valley of Flowers of the East)
subcategory: 8,000-Foot Emerald Rolling Hill Trek & Rare Dzukou Lily
description: Perched at 8,000 feet (2,452 m) altitude on the Nagaland-Manipur border, a surreal high-altitude landscape of rolling emerald green bamboo dwarf hills, meandering mountain brooks, and natural rock caves, famous for the endemic pink Dzukou Lily.
why_visit: Trek through misty moss-carpeted bamboo hills that look like a green velvet wonderland, camp in natural rocky caves under starry Himalayan skies, and spot the rare Dzukou Lily blooming in June and July.
hidden_gem_reason: A pristine, untouched high-altitude valley reached only via scenic mountain hiking trails, free from motorized vehicles and commercialization.
best_time_to_visit: June to September for flowers; October to March for crystal-clear blue skies and frosty mornings
activities: High Altitude Trekking; Wilderness Cave Camping; Endemic Floral Photography; Stargazing
distance_from_nearest_famous_place: 25 km south of Kohima (trailhead at Viswema or Jakhama)
notes: Plastic-free zone strictly enforced by SAYO (Southern Angami Youth Organisation); resthouse dormitory available at the ridge.
